scope: two equal replicated ROS 2 peers; no central coordinator

task_snapshot.subscribers: both assignment peers and passive logger
task_snapshot.role: bounded physical task proposal with source session, epoch, map revision and TTL

task_bids.publisher: assignment peer in robot N namespace
task_bids.subscribers: both assignment peers and passive logger
task_bids.role: robot-N-local Nav2 path evaluations for the current round

pair_decision.publisher: assignment peer in robot N namespace
pair_decision.subscribers: both assignment peers and passive logger
pair_decision.role: complete replicated pair assignment and score diagnostics

distributed_status.publisher: assignment peer in robot N namespace
distributed_status.subscribers: peer assignment node and passive logger
distributed_status.role: heartbeat, state, active task, health and liveness

exploration_failure.publisher: assignment peer in robot N namespace
exploration_failure.subscribers: both assignment peers and passive logger
exploration_failure.qos: reliable, transient-local, depth 1 for the node
exploration_failure.role: team-visible failure evidence and suppression hint

distributed_event.publisher: assignment peer in robot N namespace
distributed_event.role: diagnostic event stream; not a control input

identity_and_freshness.session_uuid: random per FrontierProposalAdapter process; copied into each task, snapshot and bid source provenance; assignment decisions use the source snapshot session UUID
identity_and_freshness.snapshot_epoch: monotonic per adapter candidate callback; SnapshotLedger accepts only increasing epoch within a session and rejects old retired sessions
identity_and_freshness.map_revision: source-local only; regressions within a session are rejected and cross-robot numeric comparison is forbidden
identity_and_freshness.round_id: sha256([robot1_session, robot1_epoch, robot2_session, robot2_epoch]) in fixed robot1-then-robot2 order
identity_and_freshness.union_hash: sha256(list of canonical_id in deterministic canonical task order)
identity_and_freshness.ttl: sender duration is clamped to [0.1,10] s by receive(); freshness is receiver-local steady-clock age; production launch sets snapshot 8 s, bid 8 s, decision 8 s and status 2.5 s
identity_and_freshness.bounds: snapshot <=5 tasks per source, union <=10 tasks, bid batch <=10 bids

replicated_round: Both fresh source snapshots are accepted and combined into a canonical union.
Each peer independently creates the same round_id and union_hash.
Each peer bids for up to maximum_path_queries=8 canonical tasks using its own local ComputePathToPose, reusing its own candidate-generator path when available.
Each peer publishes its local TaskBidArray; the message binds source robot, source session, source epoch, round_id, union_hash and validity.
Each peer waits for both fresh, source-consistent bid arrays, then calls choose_pair_assignment locally.
Each peer publishes the complete PairDecision including both task IDs, both bid fingerprints, epochs, score components, decision_hash and diagnostics.
A peer dispatches only after its locally computed decision matches the peer decision on peer session, round_id, union_hash, both epochs, both bid fingerprints, both assignments and decision_hash.
The local peer sends only its own selected goal; there is no peer action client, central coordinator, cmd_vel publisher or command to the other robot.
semantic_agreement: Equality of all decision-binding provenance and assignment fingerprints, not merely equality of selected coordinates or total score.
decision_hash_payload: round_id, union_hash, robot1/robot2 bid fingerprints, robot1/robot2 task IDs, and every AssignmentScore field rounded to millionths

status_and_liveness.degraded_solo: after peer snapshot timeout, a survivor can dispatch at most one local task per local snapshot epoch without coordinated claims; a new peer session is required to leave DEGRADED_SOLO
status_and_liveness.peer_session_restart: fresh peer snapshot can cancel local navigation immediately and reset the round; same old session does not recover degraded mode

protocol_preservation_answer.reason: The protocol transports bounded task identity/provenance, per-robot bid values and path samples, complete pair IDs/fingerprints, and local dispatch ownership. A replacement allocator can keep these bindings if it returns the same PairDecision contract and deterministic decision hash semantics.
protocol_preservation_answer.caveat: Changing from a scalar score to explicit visible-set utilities may require adding visible-set data or a new utility field to the task/bid messages; that is a data-model change, not a need for a central coordinator.
